question: The emergency measures to stabilise the site of the former I.A.O. S.r.l. landfill, funded for a total of EUR 24 737 449.25 under the regional operating programme Puglia 2014-2020, Axis 6 – Protecting the Environment and Promoting Natural and Cultural Resources – Action 6.2a ‘Measures to decontaminate polluted areas’, were awarded to the ad hoc consortium comprising the agent Favellato Claudio S.p.A.

and the principals Research Scarl and GECOS S.r.l.1 The owner of the company, Favellato Claudio, was involved in an investigation by the financial police (Guarda di Finanza) into wrongdoing perpetrated in 2022. The order handed down by the Rome Public Prosecutor’s Office also mentions unspecified contracts awarded to Favellato Claudio S.p.A.
; these could include the emergency measures to stabilise the site of the former I.A.O. landfill.2 In view of this: 1.
Can the Commission say whether, in its procurement for the I.A.O. landfill, Italy informed it of possible wrongdoing in the award of contracts for works funded under the Puglia 2014-2020 ROP?

Did any structural or recurring problems in the application of procurement rules or related irregularities emerge from the monitoring report that Italy sent in accordance with Article 83(3) of Directive 2014/24/EU?
Will it ask Italy for information on the practical implementation of national strategic policies on strategic procurement?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (21.6.2024) 1. The project in question is co-financed through the European Regional Development Fund under the regional operational programme Puglia 2014-2020. Italy has not informed of possible wrongdoing in the award of works contracts under this programme, thus there are no European Anti-Fraud Office (OLAF) cases on the project.
The project is implemented through various contracts, the main one being the works contract awarded in 2021 to the consortium led by the company FAVELLATO CLAUDIO Spa.

The audit authority audited the public procurement procedure and the expenditure declared to the Commission during the accounting year 2021-2022 (which comprised only the contractual advance and the related value-added tax) and did not detect any irregularity in such transactions. 2.

In the monitoring report1, Italy provided information on the most frequent sources of wrong application or of legal uncertainty2, on the level of small and medium-sized enterprises’ participation in public procurement and about prevention, detection and adequate reporting of procurement fraud, corruption, conflict of interest and other serious irregularities in the field of public procurement. 3.

In 2023, the Commission launched a project to foster the uptake of strategic public procurement in Member States. The objective is to understand the state of play for the strategic use of public procurement, identify existing barriers and potential solutions, and cooperate with local stakeholders to prepare a ‘roadmap’ towards the development of strategic public procurement.
Italy participates in the project and a workshop took place in Italy on 18 January 2024.
1 Submitted in 2021. The country monitoring reports are available at https://single-market-
economy.ec.europa.eu/single-market/public-procurement/country-reports-and-information-eu-countries_en 2 Including possible structural or recurring problems in the application of the rules.
